annotations.title: Find the right service

tools.description: Find which of ECMWF's services holds the data for a question, and get the exact tool names to call next. Returns a ranked list with the reason for each position, whether the service covers the place in the question, and the outside authority to name when the answer isn't ECMWF's to give. The services here hold data on: weather forecast for a place, past weather, forecast chart, climate projections, temperature, historical weather, meteogram, Climate DT. Use it when a question is about one of those subjects and it isn't clear which service answers. Service prefixes: forecast, reanalysis, charts, catalogue.

question.description: What the user wants to know, in their own words.

latitude.description: Latitude of the place the question is about, if there is one.

longitude.description: Longitude of the place the question is about, if there is one.

lead_time_hours.description: How far ahead the question looks, in hours. Leave it out to let the router read the horizon from the wording.

tools.name: find_service
tools.title: Find the right service

annotations.title: List services

tools.description: List ECMWF's MCP services and the outside authorities this router points to, with what each one holds, whether its output is an official product or model guidance, the area it covers and how many tools it offers. Takes no arguments.

tools.title: ECMWF forecasts: Describe a data collection

annotations.title: ECMWF forecasts: Get a weather forecast for a place

tools.description: [ECMWF forecasts] Weather forecast for one place, hour by hour: temperature, rain, wind, cloud and the other parameters published here, for the days ahead. Covers the whole world. Get the collection id and parameter ids from list_collections and describe_collection first. Returns rows by valid time in UTC, with degrees Celsius and millimetres alongside the model's own units, the model run used and the licence. Forecast model output only: no past weather, no observations, no warnings.

latitude.description: Latitude of the place the question is about, degrees north.

longitude.description: Longitude of the place the question is about, degrees east.

tools.title: ECMWF forecasts: Get a weather forecast for a place

tools.description: [ECMWF forecasts] Lowest, highest and mean value over a box on the map at one valid time, such as the warmest point in a region or how much rain covered an area. Takes a bounding box of at most 10 degrees a side, parameter ids and a valid time; returns a row per parameter with the position of each extreme, the number of grid points, the model run where there is one, and the licence. Gridded data only, not an official warning.

tools.title: ECMWF forecasts: Summarise values over an area

annotations.title: ECMWF reanalysis (ERA5): Get past weather for a place

tools.description: [ECMWF reanalysis (ERA5)] What the weather was at one place on a past date or over a past period, hour by hour or by day, since 1940: temperature, rain, wind, cloud, pressure and the other parameters published here. Covers the whole world, hourly since 1940. Takes a latitude and longitude, parameter ids, and start and end as ISO dates or date-times; set daily=true for per-day lowest, highest and mean values, and totals for rain and the radiation fluxes. One call covers at most 366 days; do not split multi-year analyses into parallel calls. Returns rows by valid time in UTC, with degrees Celsius and millimetres alongside the source units and the licence. The record stops about 6 days behind real time: no forecasts, no station observations, no warnings.

latitude.description: Latitude of the place the question is about, degrees north.

longitude.description: Longitude of the place the question is about, degrees east.

start.description: First date or time to report, ISO 8601, e.g. 1976-07-01.

end.description: Last date or time to report; a date means the whole UTC day.

level.description: Pressure level in hPa, for a collection that has levels.

daily.description: Summarise each UTC day instead of returning every time.

annotations.title: ECMWF charts: Find a forecast chart

tools.description: [ECMWF charts] Search the catalogue of official forecast charts by what a chart shows, for example 'mean sea level pressure', 'rain', '2 m temperature' or 'wave height'. Returns the product name to pass to get_chart, what each chart shows, and the inputs it takes: the areas it can be drawn on, how far ahead it runs, and the model runs on offer. It also lists the map layers get_map can draw. Start here when you don't already know the product name. It returns a catalogue, not an image.

query.description: What the chart shows, in plain words, e.g. 'mean sea level pressure'.

limit.description: How many products to return, at most 12.

tools.name: charts_find_charts
tools.title: ECMWF charts: Find a forecast chart

annotations.title: ECMWF charts: Get a forecast chart

tools.description: [ECMWF charts] One official forecast chart as an image, the same chart as on the charts website: pressure, wind, temperature, rain, cloud, waves and the rest of the catalogue. Takes a product name from find_charts, a step in hours ahead or a valid time, and an area such as europe or global; the model run is the latest that has the step unless you name one. Returns the picture with its base time, valid time, area, the page it came from and its licence. The areas are the ones the product publishes, so for a bounding box of your own use get_map. It's a picture of model output, not a table of numbers and not an official warning.

product.description: Product name from find_charts, e.g. medium-mslp-wind850.

step.description: Hours after the model run the chart should show, e.g. 36.

valid_time.description: The moment the chart should show, ISO 8601 UTC, e.g. 2026-10-10T12:00:00Z.

base_time.description: Model run to draw from, ISO 8601 UTC; the latest one by default.

area.description: Area the chart is drawn on, e.g. europe, global, north_america.

tools.name: charts_get_chart
tools.title: ECMWF charts: Get a forecast chart

annotations.title: ECMWF charts: Get an ensemble meteogram for a place

tools.description: [ECMWF charts] The official ensemble meteogram for one place: how the 51-member ensemble forecast spreads over the next 10 or 15 days for cloud, rain, wind and temperature, drawn as one image. Takes a latitude and longitude anywhere in the world and a place name to label it. Kinds: 10-day, 15-day, 15-day-with-climate, plume, wave. Use it for how confident a forecast for a place is, and how the weather there changes day by day. It answers with a picture of the ensemble, not with numbers, and it isn't an official warning.

latitude.description: Latitude of the place the question is about, degrees north.

longitude.description: Longitude of the place the question is about, degrees east.

place_name.description: Name of the place, used to label the meteogram.

base_time.description: Model run to draw from, ISO 8601 UTC; the latest one by default.

tools.name: charts_get_meteogram
tools.title: ECMWF charts: Get an ensemble meteogram for a place

annotations.title: ECMWF charts: Get a forecast map for an area

tools.description: [ECMWF charts] A forecast map for a bounding box you choose, drawn by the Web Map Service: mean sea level pressure, 500 hPa geopotential, 850 hPa temperature and wind speed, and the ensemble mean and spread of each. Takes west, south, east and north in degrees and either a valid time or a step in hours ahead, and returns the map with a background, coastlines and borders, and the legend where the layer has one. Layers: msl_mean_public, msl_public, msl_spread_public, t850_mean_public, t850_public, t850_spread_public, ws850_mean_public, ws850_public, ws850_spread_public, z500_mean_public, z500_public, z500_spread_public. Use it when the area wanted isn't one of the areas get_chart offers. These layers hold no surface temperature, rain or 10 m wind; those are chart products.

layer.description: Map layer name, e.g. msl_public or t850_public.

west.description: Western edge of the map, degrees east of Greenwich.

south.description: Southern edge of the map, degrees north.

east.description: Eastern edge of the map, degrees east of Greenwich.

north.description: Northern edge of the map, degrees north.

valid_time.description: The moment the chart should show, ISO 8601 UTC, e.g. 2026-10-10T12:00:00Z.

step.description: Hours ahead of the latest analysis to draw.

style.description: Style for the layer; its first style by default.

tools.name: charts_get_map
tools.title: ECMWF charts: Get a forecast map for an area

tools.title: Destination Earth data catalogue: Describe dataset

annotations.title: Destination Earth data catalogue: Get axes

tools.description:
[Destination Earth data catalogue] Return the axes (MARS keys) of a dataset for the CURRENT selection branch.

        For every axis: label, description, selected values, the number of valid
        options given the other selections, and either the labelled `options`
        (selectable axes) or a `summary` with the min..max extent (large axes,
        e.g. dates: choose a range inside it). `invalid` lists selected values
        that are not available with the rest of the selection, and
        `unset_axes` lists axes that still have more than one option.

        `selection` maps MARS keys to a code or list of codes, e.g.
        {"stream": "clmn", "param": ["167"], "year": ["2020", "2021"]}.
tools.name: catalogue_get_axes
tools.title: Destination Earth data catalogue: Get axes

annotations.title: Destination Earth data catalogue: Probe availability

tools.description:
[Destination Earth data catalogue] Read-only "what if" check. Each query is
        {"axis": "param", "under": {"stream": ["clmn"]}, "target": "133"}: it
        reports whether `target` is a valid option of `axis` if the `under`
        values replaced the current `selection` (axes after them are cleared),
        and how many options that axis would have. Probe both sides of a
        branching choice before committing to it.
tools.name: catalogue_probe_availability
tools.title: Destination Earth data catalogue: Probe availability

tools.description:
[Destination Earth data catalogue] Turn a selection into the minimal list of valid MARS requests, plus
        the DestinE data locations (Polytope endpoints) that can serve them.
        Single-valued axes are filled in automatically; check `unset_axes`
        (axes you left open, which the request then spans entirely).
tools.name: catalogue_build_mars_requests
tools.title: Destination Earth data catalogue: Build mars requests

tools.name: catalogue_destine_authentication_help
tools.title: Destination Earth data catalogue: Destine authentication help

annotations.title: Destination Earth data catalogue: Retrieve data

tools.description:
[Destination Earth data catalogue] Retrieve the data for a selection from DestinE Polytope.

        The server rebuilds the MARS requests from the selection and fetches
        each field from one data location that serves it (data split across
        locations is fetched from each; replicated data only once), or only
        from `location` if given. It runs the retrieval and
        returns one download URL per request, reusable until it expires (GRIB, or CoverageJSON
        when the request has a `feature`).

        Authentication: preferably the MCP client sends a DestinE token in the
        `X-DestinE-Token` header (see destine_authentication_help). Only as a
        last resort pass `destine_token` here — the token then passes through
        the chat/LLM. Never ask the user for their DestinE password.
tools.name: catalogue_retrieve_data
tools.title: Destination Earth data catalogue: Retrieve data
